description: Historical baseline of optical probing limits — manually curated. The DREAM 'pixel is real' claim predicts the curve should saturate at the kernel's λ_q (a structural cutoff that no engineering can push lower). Standard physics predicts the boundary keeps moving with engineering progress. The tracker tests which is right.

baseline_records.source: Abbe, E. (1873) Beiträge zur Theorie des Mikroskops
Pohl et al. (1984) — first NSOM demonstrations
Betzig et al., Rust et al. (2006) — Nobel 2014
LIGO O4 sensitivity ~10^-19 m / sqrt(Hz), 10^-14 m cumulative

baseline_records.technique: Theoretical 'pixel sees field discolouration' limit (DREAM kernel pixel)
baseline_records.source: DREAM A6 — claimed structural cutoff of the projection kernel

dream_prediction.claim: The pixel is real — λ_q is a structural property of the projection kernel, not an engineering limit
dream_prediction.falsifiable_prediction: Resolution curve flattens (saturates at the kernel's λ_q) — no amount of engineering pushes λ_q lower
dream_prediction.standard_physics_prediction: Resolution curve keeps dropping with engineering improvements — no structural floor
dream_prediction.current_status: Untested — daily scout tracks new published limits to detect whether saturation occurs
